facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support the diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma.

The presence of cytokeratin8/18-positive and MNF116-positive tumor cells in the sentinel lymph node and the lack of evidence of primary or secondary tumors in the chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans suggest the possibility of metastatic breast cancer.

The presence of multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor-positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration may suggest apocrine gland hyperplasia, although this is less likely given the overall clinical and histopathological picture.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, along with the lack of evidence of primary or secondary tumors in the chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, suggest the possibility of cutaneous metastasis of unknown primary.
